text: The mist thickens around your ankles, then — without hurry — draws back. Somewhere in the valley, a chime sounds once; you have been noticed.
The hidden frogs fall silent in a ragged wave. Something large is moving in the rocks above. Then, one by one, the frogs begin again, louder than before.
A black lotus unfurls at your passing, its petals slick as wet glass. It breathes out once — a cold, sweet breath — and you feel a small gate open somewhere beneath your ribs.
